newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police raid Satanic sect in child search. [CORRECTED 14:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Belgian police raid Satanic sect in child search. [CORRECTED 14:42 GMT]

text.p: Police investigating a Belgian gang accused of child sexual abuse and murder raided the headquarters of a Satanic sect at the weekend looking for clues, RTBF television reported on Monday.
It said 150 police and special investigators raided the headquarters of the Institut Abrasax in Forchies-La-Marche, near the central Belgian city of Charleroi, on Saturday night.
The television showed police taking away bags of papers, video cassettes and a refrigerator. It said they also took away black magic ritual implements and human skulls.

RTBF said the raid had been prompted by the discovery of an undated letter addressed to someone named Bernard asking him to remind someone else that a special ceremony was approaching and to remember a "special gift".
The letter was signed by "Anubis", an ancient Egyptian god and the assumed name of the high priest of the Abrasax sect.
Frenchman Bernard Weinstein was an accomplice of a gang led by convicted rapist Marc Dutroux, who has admitted killing him.

Weinstein's body was found alongside those of eight-year-olds Julie Lejeune and Melissa Russo in mid-August, buried on a property belonging to Dutroux in the town of Sars-La-Buissiere south-west of Charleroi.
The two girls, abducted in June 1995 (corrects from 1996), had starved to death earlier this year.
Dominique Kindermans, the high priestess of the sect, said that to her knowledge neither Dutroux nor Weinstein had ever been members of, or connected with, Abrasax.

A spokesman for gendarmes searching an abandoned mine complex in nearby Jumet, a suburb of Charleroi, refused to comment on any link between the Abrasax raid and their own hunt for a secret hiding place they are convinced Dutroux had in the mine for abducted children.
Dutroux once lived in a caravan near the mine complex.
On Monday gendarmes working in glacial conditions focused their attentions on a partially flooded chamber in one of the mine galleries that they discovered at the weekend.
Acting on statements by Dutroux and his second wife Michelle Martin, police have been searching the mine since December 13.

Dutroux and several alleged accomplices have been detained since August after two young girls were rescued alive from a makeshift dungeon hidden in the basement of a house he owned in the Charleroi suburb of Marcinelle.

Two days later the bodies of Julie and Melissa were found. Barely two weeks after that police dug up the remains of An Marchal and Eefje Lambrecks under a shed in the grounds of a house in Charleroi formerly occupied by Weinstein.
In October more than 250,000 people marched through Brussels in support of the victims and their parents as well as to demonstrate their anger at failings in the judicial system.

Police are still searching for at least seven other children who have gone missing over the past eight years. A special parliamentary commission is hearing evidence from police, gendarmes and magistrates over how investigations were handled.
In the case of Julie and Melissa, gendarmes and the magistrates each accuse the other of bungling.
